company_stage: large public semiconductor and manufacturing company

culture_principles.name: Public mission and customer-impact alignment
culture_principles.description: Intel fit should connect work to the company outcomes and users described in cited public sources.

culture_principles.name: Evidence-backed execution
culture_principles.description: Strong answers should show practical judgment, clear tradeoffs, ownership, and outcomes rather than generic enthusiasm.

culture_principles.name: Engineering discipline at manufacturing scale
culture_principles.description: Public material ties product claims to process, yield, and validation realities, so answers that ignore manufacturability read as incomplete.

culture_principles.name: Quality and security before schedule
culture_principles.description: Chip-level defects propagate at scale, which makes verification and security review structural rather than final-stage gates.

culture_principles.name: Responsible innovation beyond the product
culture_principles.description: Public careers material frames technology work around responsible innovation, sustainability, and community impact alongside product delivery.

hiring_signals.signal: Connects decisions to the users, customers, products, or markets named in public company sources.
Uses concrete examples to show ownership, learning, and measurable improvement.
Shows a debugging or validation process where evidence narrowed the search space step by step.
Explains a handoff between design, process, and test teams and what made it reliable.
Describes owning quality outcomes beyond their own deliverable, including coverage or escape analysis.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Generic admiration for the company without a concrete role, customer, product, or business mechanism.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public lens usage should stay grounded in cited source signals and role-relevant evidence.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Assuming every Intel role is chip design and ignoring manufacturing, validation, software, and business roles.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public sources describe a broad set of role families with different constraints.

anti_signals.anti_signal: Performance claims without a baseline, workload definition, or measurement method.
anti_signals.risk_reason: Public product messaging is benchmark-oriented, so unsupported claims cannot be evaluated.

interview_patterns.pattern: Use cited public source signals to test role-relevant judgment, ownership, communication, and impact.

honest_limits: This is a lightweight public-source lens and does not represent an official Intel hiring standard.
It contains source metadata and non-verbatim public-safe signals only.
Role, team, seniority, location, and hiring manager can materially change interview emphasis.
This lens requires deeper multi-source validation before being promoted to FULLY_DISTILLED.
